Adds a required `AcpEventLedger.close()` hook, implements it for SQLite and in-memory ledgers, and calls it from ACP gateway shutdown after tracking in-flight gateway event handlers for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100637.

PR surface: Source +27. Total +27 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows current main has no ACP SQLite ledger close on shutdown, and the current PR head puts that close behind an unbounded in-flight event drain; I did not run tests in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(acp): add close() to SQLite event ledger and release on shutdown (#100637)
target.body:
Fixes #100637.

## What Problem This Solves

`createSqliteAcpEventLedger()` in `src/acp/event-ledger.ts` opens a SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection through `openOpenClawStateDatabase()` but never exposes a way to close it. During ACP gateway hot-reload or shutdown, the cached handle survives in `cachedDatabases`, causing SQLite file lock contention when the new process attempts to reopen the same database.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Added `close()` to `AcpEventLedger` interface — SQLite ledger calls `closeOpenClawStateDatabase()`, in-memory/API ledger provides a no-op
2. Wired `eventLedger.close()` into `serveAcpGateway` shutdown handler (SIGINT/SIGTERM + error paths)
3. Follows the same lifecycle pattern already used by `plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts`, `task-registry.store.sqlite.ts`, and `task-flow-registry.store.sqlite.ts`

All `AcpEventLedger` implementations now satisfy the lifecycle contract — the in-memory ledger (used by `createLedgerApi()` and `createInMemoryAcpEventLedger()`) has a no-op `close()`, consistent with the interface requirement.

## Evidence

### 1. Live Gateway Environment

```
$ openclaw gateway status
Service: systemd user (enabled)
Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789
Runtime: running (pid 1402, state active)
Connectivity probe: ok
```

### 2. BEFORE vs AFTER — File Descriptor Leak Proof (current head ee7a9af)

```
$ node --import tsx/esm scripts/repro-100637-ledger-close.mjs
=======================================================
Issue #100637: ACP event ledger close() proof
=======================================================

--- [BEFORE] No close() method ---
  FDs before create: 31
  FDs after read():   34 (delta: +3)
  --> [CRITICAL_FAIL] LEDGER HAS NO CLOSE — handles leak on shutdown

--- [AFTER] ledger.close() releases handles ---
  FDs before create:   31
  FDs after read():    34 (delta: +3)
  FDs after close():   31 (delta: -3)
  --> [SUCCESS] close() releases handles, clean shutdown

=======================================================
RESULT: BEFORE/AFTER PROOF PASSED
=======================================================
```

### 3. Regression Tests (current head ee7a9af)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/server.startup.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

### 4. Full Lifecycle Audit

**Open path**: `createSqliteAcpEventLedger()` → `read()` → `openOpenClawStateDatabase()` → `new DatabaseSync(path)` → cached in `cachedDatabases` Map

**Close path (before fix)**: NOTHING — `cachedDatabases` survives process signals

**Close path (after fix)**: `serveAcpGateway.shutdown()` → `eventLedger?.close()` → `closeOpenClawStateDatabase()` → iterates `cachedDatabases`, calls `db.close()` + `walMaintenance.close()`, clears cache

**Contract completeness (P1 fix)**:
| Ledger implementation | `close()` provided? |
|---|---|
| SQLite (`createSqliteAcpEventLedger`) | ✅ calls `closeOpenClawStateDatabase()` |
| In-memory (`createLedgerApi` / `createInMemoryAcpEventLedger`) | ✅ no-op (no persistent resources) |

After analyzing `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts#L972-L998`, we verify that `closeOpenClawStateDatabase()` correctly closes every cached `DatabaseSync` instance, calls `walMaintenance.close()` for WAL cleanup, and clears the cache.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/server.startup.test.ts --run` — 12/12 passed
- `scripts/repro-100637-ledger-close.mjs` — BEFORE/AFTER PASSED
- Gateway live: running, probe ok

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
